A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same q-exponential policy optimization study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original online control experiments, offline D4RL evaluations and policy-evolution analyses in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 reports original online and offline evaluations in Section 5 and Appendix E, including revised results and an added boundary-density analysis.

M1.justification: The policy families, learned Student's t degrees of freedom, actor losses and nearest in-support action replacement are retained. V2 Algorithms 1–2 formalize sampling and action handling already described in v1 Appendix B; they do not establish new procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate continuous Mountain Car, Pendulum and Acrobot, plus the same nine D4RL datasets spanning HalfCheetah, Hopper and Walker2d at three data-quality levels. The added boundary analysis uses an existing Walker2d scenario.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparator sets are unchanged, including appendix TD3BC comparisons. However, v1 Figures 5/14 label the policy-evolution comparator Squashed Gaussian, whereas v2 Figure 9/Table 3 label it Gaussian while nearby prose still says Squashed Gaussian. The PDFs do not resolve whether that comparator actually changed.

E3.justification: The evaluation framework is retained, but selected offline settings change. For example, IQL's heavy-tailed q-Gaussian learning rate on Walker2d-medium-replay changes from 0.0003 to 0.003, and TAWAC's heavy-tailed q-Gaussian temperature on Hopper-medium changes from 0.01 to 0.50. V2 also introduces AUC-based comparative summaries. These reported revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 Table 3 adds an analysis of density accumulating at action boundaries, extending the Walker2d policy-evolution case study. V1 Figure 6's comparison of generated samples with theoretical q-Gaussian densities is removed. Most existing policy-evolution analysis is retained or relocated.

E5.justification: V2 Section 5 adds a general five-seed sweep/ten-seed final-evaluation statement, while its retained online appendix still specifies 30 final seeds. Offline five/ten-seed reporting and standard-error/interquartile-range conventions remain unchanged. Seed reporting changes, but actual run-count changes cannot be established.

E6.justification: Offline boxplots, aggregate comparisons and learning curves are revised across algorithms. For example, Figure 18's InAC Student's t curve on Hopper-medium-expert ends around 85–90 in v1 versus 60–65 in v2, alongside a changed reported learning rate. V2 additionally reports online AUC win counts, an offline aggregate and boundary-density values. These are substantial revised or newly reported outcomes, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 2 corrects the q-logarithm denominator from 1−1 to 1−q. V1's explicit sparsemax threshold and special quadratic-policy derivations are removed. The main Tsallis-regularization mathematics moves to Appendix B, while Appendix A's gradient derivations remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims remain: tractable q-exponential policies can improve existing actor-critic algorithms, Student's t is comparatively stable, and heavy-tailed q-Gaussian works favorably with TAWAC. The rewritten contributions emphasize explicit policy parameterization without materially changing these claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds boundary concentration as a possible explanation for TAWAC performance and skewness as an explanation for Beta's Mountain Car performance. Its limitations remove the proposed large-scale initialization/annealing remedy and add the dimensional difficulty of exact boundary projection. The offline failure of light-tailed policies remains acknowledged.

D1.justification: V2 documents action clipping without density correction, empirical entropy approximation, IQL's 0.7 expectile and a full offline temperature table. It also specifies an exception to mean bounding for offline Gaussian policies. Conversely, the code-access link in v1's abstract is removed. These disclosures do not by themselves establish implementation changes.

R1.justification: The introduction and Table 1 shift emphasis from competing q-exponential conventions to explicit versus implicit policy parameterization, reclassifying several prior RL methods as continuous but implicit. Citation changes include adding Chow et al. 2018b and removing Garg et al. 2023 and Martins and Astudillo 2016; the overall research positioning remains recognizable.

P1.justification: The introduction, background, distribution discussion and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten and reorganized. Entropy regularization moves from the main text to Appendix B, while sampling and actor-critic integration receive prominent main-text treatment. Appendix organization, terminology and author information also change.

P2.justification: V2 consolidates three online learning-curve figures into Figure 4, adds summary plots and Table 3, brings the six-dimensional policy-evolution display into the main text, and introduces two algorithm boxes. Related-work and policy tables are redesigned, and the temperature table is substantially expanded. These changes extend well beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the study easier to follow and implement through clearer algorithm integration, consolidated online comparisons and fuller clipping and hyperparameter documentation. The new summaries and boundary analysis add interpretive value. These limited gains are tempered by removal of the code link and unresolved seed-count and Gaussian-comparator inconsistencies; revised scores do not establish same-setting improvements.
